metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Back on the Waiver Radar After Leading Browns in Receiving?
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is only rostered in 4% of Yahoo leagues at the moment, but that number could be going north by the end of the week after his four-catch, 69-yard game in Sunday's 13-10 Week 6 win over the division-rival Baltimore Ravens. Jeudy led the team in receiving, and it was also his highest yardage total through the first six weeks. The 27-year-old former first-rounder from Alabama did very little in the team's first five games, catching eight of his 15 targets for 81 yards and no trips to the end zone. He even had back-to-back contests in Weeks 2 and 3 where he gave fantasy managers a zero on the scoresheet. The disappointing part about his good game on Sunday is that his four targets were third on the team, and rookie pass-catchers KC Concepcion Jr. and Denzel Boston are both healthy and should continue to be the primary weapons for veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson. It was nice to see Jeudy get more involved for Cleveland in an impressive divisional upset, but most fantasy managers will want to see more in an offense that is definitely not turning any heads so far.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy paces Cleveland in yards in Week 6
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy caught four passes for a team-high 69 yards in a Week 6 win against Baltimore.
metadata.analysis: Jeudy had his biggest game of the season so far, catching every target for a season-high in yardage. His name has been thrown around in trade rumors after the Browns' rookie wideouts started strong, but he has value as the team's WR3, even if he is not a reliable fantasy producer.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy - Leads team in receiving in Week 6 win
metadata.description: Jeudy caught all four targets for 69 yards in Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Jeudy's four targets were third on the team, but he made the most of them and ended up leading the Browns in receiving on a day Deshaun Watson threw for just 164 yards and no touchdowns. The veteran wideout entered Week 6 with just eight catches for 81 yards and can largely be ignored in fantasy as Cleveland's fourth or fifth option on offense most weeks.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Named as Possible Trade Candidate
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is a name to watch as a potential trade candidate, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano. Jeudy has caught just eight of 15 targets for 81 yards in five games this season, ranking sixth among Browns players. With the emergence of rookie wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, Jeudy's usage has decreased in 2026, except in Week 5, when Concepcion left early with a concussion. The former first-round pick has totaled over 800 yards in three of his first six years, including a 1,229-yard season in 2024 with the Browns. While it's unclear whether Jeudy will be traded or which landing spots to watch, fantasy managers should keep an eye on this situation.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy an Interesting Stash Option
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is someone worth looking at on the waiver wire ahead of Week 6. This past weekend, Jeudy hauled in three of his seven targets for 19 yards during the loss to the New York Jets. The seven targets were a season-high for Jeudy, who has struggled to get involved at times. The Browns could be looking his way more frequently with KC Concepcion (concussion) uncertain for the Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. According to Jordan Schultz, the Browns are attempting to move Jeudy ahead of the trade deadline. The 27-year-old is an intriguing stash option, given a possible bigger role or move elsewhere soon.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy could be traded by Browns
metadata.description: The Browns are reportedly seeking a third or fourth-round pick for WR Jerry Jeudy.
metadata.analysis: Jordan Schultz reported he's not sure they'll be able to get it. Jeudy will be a player to monitor closer to the trade deadline.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Available With Trade Deadline Approaching
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns veteran wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is available with the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, according to Jordan Schultz, with the Browns looking for something in the early third- to fourth-round range in return. It is unclear if the Browns will be able to get that in return for a declining pass-catcher, but what is clear is that Cleveland is excited about their young receiver group of KC Concepcion Jr., Denzel Boston, and Isaiah Bond. The 27-year-old Jeudy, the former 15th overall pick by the Denver Broncos in 2020 from Alabama, has caught only eight of his 15 targets for 81 yards and no touchdowns through five games in 2026 in his third year in Cleveland. Jeudy played a season-high 81% of the offensive snaps in the Week 5 loss to the New York Jets on Sunday, but that was likely only because Concepcion left the game early with a concussion. He played only 38% of the offensive snaps the week prior in the Thursday night win over the division-rival Pittsburgh Steelers. A trade out of town might be the only thing that makes fantasy managers consider adding Jeudy to their rosters off the waiver wire again this year.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy - Unproductive in loss
metadata.description: Jeudy hauled in three of seven targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 17-12 loss against the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Quarterback Deshaun Watson struggled mightily against a tough Jets defense in Week 5, completing just 15 of his 33 pass attempts for 155 yards and getting sacked eight times. Jeudy's production still managed to lag behind even that baseline, as he averaged fewer than three yards per target Sunday. He'll be hoping to at least keep up the target volume in a Week 6 matchup versus the Ravens.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy catches three passes in Week 5
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy caught three of his seven targets for 19 yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Jeudy tied for the lead with seven targets, but he wasn't able to do much with the opportunities. The veteran wideout has been quiet through the first five games of the season, catching just eight passes for 81 yards. He will not be a recommended fantasy option in Week 6 against Baltimore

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy has Become an Afterthought
metadata.description: While two Cleveland Browns wide receivers have thrived in their first professional seasons, veteran wide receiver Jerry Jeudy has been left out in the cold by quarterback Deshaun Watson. Jeudy has just five receptions for 62 yards on the season, an average of 12.4 yards per reception. He has yet to find the end zone and is currently behind two running backs, Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders, in targets, receptions, and yards receiving. Jeudy has not seen ample opportunity and, as a result, is RotoBaller's 89th-ranked wide receiver. He is projected to score just three fantasy points against the Jets this week.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Could Be a Trade Target for Receiver-Needy NFL Contenders
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns veteran wide receiver Jerry Jeudy has caught only five passes through the first four weeks of the 2026 season, and NFL insider Adam Schefter believes he could be a potential trade candidate ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline. The Browns have spent significant draft capital to get younger and more explosive at the skill positions, and the emergence of rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion has made Jeudy an afterthought in the offense only two seasons after recording a career-high 1,229 receiving yards in his first year with the team. Jeudy's contract runs through 2027, but with a manageable cap hit, the 27-year-old could find more involvement with a receiver-needy contender, with Schefter specifically floating the Kansas City Chiefs as a potential fit.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy - Shows life late in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Jeudy caught all three of his targets for 36 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over Pittsburgh.
metadata.analysis: It looked like Jeudy could be shut out for the third straight game after finishing the first half with no targets. However, the veteran wideout gave Cleveland a first down with a nine-yard reception late in the third quarter, then came up with two big catches -- a 17-yarder and a 10-yarder -- after the two-minute warning in the fourth to help set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. The two fourth-quarter catches alone accounted for more yardage than Jeudy had recorded across his first three games of the campaign, so perhaps he and QB Deshaun Watson have found some chemistry that they can carry over into a Week 5 matchup versus the Jets.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy hauls in three passes Thursday night
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy caught all three of his targets in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: After catching no passes with just one target over the last two weeks, Jeudy got involved again on Thursday night. He was still targeted just three times while playing only 24 snaps. Jeudy should remain on the waiver wire in all but the deepest of fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy - Doesn't draw any targets in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Jeudy finished Sunday's 21-18 victory against Carolina with no targets or touches.
metadata.analysis: It was the second straight week that Jeudy didn't log a reception, and this time he didn't even get a target (he logged just one in Week 2 versus Tampa Bay). The veteran wideout continues to be on the field fairly often -- he's recorded an offensive snap share of over 50 percent in each of the Browns' three contests, including Sunday, when he played 51 percent of the team's offensive snaps. However, he doesn't seem to be clicking well with QB Deshaun Watson, and at this point fantasy managers have little reason to include him in their lineups.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy again catchless in win Sunday
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy was held without a target or touch in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was not able to contribute on Sunday, failing to see a single opportunity in the team's win over the Panthers. He seems to have entirely fallen behind the rookies in Cleveland's receiving room and won't be fantasy relevant moving forward.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Not Getting Enough Looks In Passing Game
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy has not been heavily involved in the Browns passing attack thus far through two games of the season and cannot be trusted as a fantasy wide receiver play until he shows more. He should not be used this week in a matchup against the Carolina Panthers. Jeudy has seen five total targets this season and has two catches for 26 receiving yards. That's not enough involvement to make him fantasy relevant and until he develops more of a chemistry with Deshaun Watson, he should remain on the bench. Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, although both rookies, have emerged as the two main pass-catching targets in Cleveland as well as the tight end Harold Fannin Jr. Coming into the season, it was expected that Jeudy might have a role in the passing game as the second or third receiver as the veteran, but that really hasn't developed yet. Until further notice Jeudy can't be trusted to return fantasy results.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy - Blanked by Tampa Bay
metadata.description: Jeudy failed to haul in his lone target during the Browns' 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Jeudy couldn't improve on his 2-26-0 receiving line (on four targets) during the Browns' Week 1 loss to the Jaguars. The seventh-year pro played 34 of 58 offensive snaps Sunday (58.6 percent), third-most among Cleveland wide receivers behind rookies Denzel Boston (54) and KC Concepcion (38). Jeudy finished the 2025 regular season with the second-most receiving yards on the Browns, but it appears Boston, Concepcion, tight end Harold Fannin and even running back Quinshon Judkins are the preferred targets for Deshaun Watson to open the season. Jeudy will look for better results in Cleveland's home opener against Carolina on Sept. 27.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy held without catch Sunday
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy did not catch his lone target in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: Denzel Boston has emerged as the WR1 on the Browns offense. Jeudy remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Not Worthy of Start in Week 2 Matchup at Bucs
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy was not heavily involved in Game 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He caught two passes for 26 yards on four targets and was outplayed by fellow wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. That could be the case again in Week 2 when the Browns visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Look for Jeudy to be third in line in the wide receiver pecking order behind Boston and Concepcion. He could get a few targets, but will have to make the most of those targets in order to make an impact at the Buccaneers. The Bucs defense is very solid and did a good job of keeping Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and the Bengals receivers in check in Week 1. The Bucs have a young but talented secondary that should do a good job of defending Jeudy and limiting his output in Week 2. If you need to start a Browns receiver, it might be the smart move to look towards Boston or Concepcion rather than Jeudy this week.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: Jeudy is going to be good to go on Sunday, which was expected after he was able to practice without limitations this week. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for however long Deshaun Watson is starting for the Browns, however.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) logs full practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout tweaked his wrist recently, but it doesn't seem to be a serious issue, as he was still able to practice in full on Wednesday. He should play this week but doesn't project to be a good fantasy option in a matchup against the Buccaneers.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy - Logs two catches in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Jeudy caught two passes on four targets for 26 yards during the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Jeudy's first target from Deshaun Watson in the first quarter resulted in an interception, leading to a 30-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to Parker Washington. Jeudy and Watson connected on passes of 20 and six yards late in the second quarter, but the sixth-year wide receiver did not see a target in the second half. His 32 snaps on offense were third-most behind rookies Denzel Boston (47) and KC Concepcion (35), and Jeudy is also competing with tight end Harold Fannin for targets. Up next is a Week 2 road clash against the Buccaneers on Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy catches two passes in loss
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy caught two of four targets for 26 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Jeudy's four targets tied him with Denzel Boston for second on the team behind KC Concepcion, but he didn't have much to show for it. Cleveland struggled to move the ball all day, leading to many short drives and little opportunity for the offensive players to get any momentum. Hopefully, things will turn more in a positive direction next week against the Bucs.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Should Stay on Benches in Week 1
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy enters Week 1 with a starting job, but not much fantasy security. He drew 106 targets last season and turned them into 50 catches for 602 yards and two touchdowns. Harold Fannin Jr. actually led Cleveland with 107 targets, and now first-round rookie KC Concepcion Jr. and second-rounder Denzel Boston are both starting too. That leaves Jeudy fighting for work in an offense led by Deshaun Watson, which is enough to make Sunday's matchup with Jacksonville hard to trust. The Jaguars allowed 3,707 passing yards and 25 passing touchdowns last season, but they also picked off 22 passes. RotoBaller has Jeudy at WR77 for Week 1, and its current start-sit guidance recommends Cleveland's receivers only in deeper leagues with multiple flex spots. Jeudy may still see enough snaps to matter, but there are too many questions about the target split and quarterback play. He should stay on the bench in most leagues.

metadata.title: Jerry Jeudy Losing Ground to the Browns' Youth Movement
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is quickly falling out of favor as some of his younger teammates ascend into substantial roles. Jeudy had a miserable fantasy campaign in 2025, catching 50 passes for 602 yards and two touchdowns. While part of his subpar season can be blamed on quarterback play, Jeudy deserves to take on a substantial amount of accountability. He has ranked as the WR47 or lower in four of his six NFL seasons, serving as a major letdown to fantasy managers who trusted him with the Broncos or Browns. Now, Cleveland's front office is losing faith in him, as they drafted KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston to be the future of their receiver room. Jeudy may still earn the start in Week 1, but his vastly reduced role and poor quarterback play mean that he belongs on the bench (or even the waiver wire) in most fantasy football leagues.

metadata.title: New Role, Crowded Depth Chart in Cleveland Clouds Jerry Jeudy's Value
metadata.description: Jerry Jeudy is listed as a starting wide receiver for Week 1 on the Cleveland Browns' depth chart, but his exact role remains uncertain. Cleveland head coach Todd Monken is expected to move Jeudy around as a Z or F receiver, instead of his usual role as an X, which is generally considered a team's No. 1 wideout. However, Monken noted that Jeudy could still play as the X as well. With rookie Denzel Boston now expected to play the X spot, fellow rookie wideout KC Concepcion also emerging as a starter, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. expected to remain heavily involved, Jeudy may not see as many targets as he did last season (106). Jeudy ranked second on Cleveland in 2025 with receptions (50) and receiving yards (602), behind Fannin. He also scored just two touchdowns. Jeudy, RotoBaller's No. 77 wide receiver (half-PPR), is currently rostered in just 12% of Yahoo leagues, but is somebody to monitor in the later rounds of upcoming fantasy football drafts.
